title: Quantitative Assessment of Crystal Structure Prediction
claim: The benchmark evaluates predictions through a staged protocol of retrieving all valid reference variants and scoring against the closest, treating two task types separately.
layout: Single winding flow band right-to-left, 4 numbered stages, input-type inset top-right
description: A large curved grey-blue ribbon sweeps from the right side to the left, carrying 3D ball-and-stick crystal structures through four numbered, dashed-circle stages. (1) Prediction: a single predicted crystal. (2) Polymorphs Retrieval: the prediction is shown beside several ground-truth polymorphs labeled GT1, GT2 and GTn. (3) Geometric Alignment: two structures are aligned side by side. (4) Polymorph Selection: GT1 is kept solid and the other candidates fade out. The title 'OPAL-Bench' is in large bold serif at the top center, with a short blurb about 7 CSP and 2 SICSP models. The top-left has a '4 Datasets' pill and an 'Evaluation Metrics' label above a ranked bar chart (GT1 is the shortest bar, highlighted in blue). The top-right gray inset lists the input types for SICSP and CSP: space group and Wyckoff positions, atom species, random cell, and random coordinates. Red, pink and blue atoms are the main colors.
caption: OPAL-Bench evaluation pipeline. OPAL-Bench evaluates seven CSP and two SICSP methods across four datasets, with four geometric and five physical metrics, treating CSP and SICSP as fundamentally distinct tasks. For each composition, a model predicts one structure, and we retrieve all known polymorphs, the distinct stable structures of the same composition, as candidate references. We then apply species-aware SE(3) alignment for geometric metrics, while physical metrics are SE(3)-invariant and require no alignment, and score each metric against its closest polymorph.
abstract: Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP) aims to predict a material's 3D structure from its chemical composition, with applications from energy storage to biomedical devices. Despite its importance, existing evaluation frameworks suffer from key limitations: they rely on threshold-sensitive or incomparable metrics, focus predominantly on geometric performance while overlooking physical plausibility, and fail to account for polymorphism, where a chemical composition can crystallize into multiple stable structures. In parallel, recent Symmetry-Informed CSP (SICSP) methods often report results alongside standard CSP baselines while receiving crystallographic templates at inference, which constrain the search space and make SICSP a fundamentally different task. To address these limitations, we introduce an Orientation-invariant, Polymorph-Aware, Large Benchmark (OPAL-Bench) that evaluates CSP and SICSP as separate tasks. We evaluate 7 CSP and 2 SICSP methods under OPAL-Bench across 4 datasets using threshold-free geometric and physical distance metrics. Our results show that no method dominates across all metrics, and that geometric performance is not strongly correlated with physical plausibility. We also release OPAL-CSP, an SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching baseline for the CSP track that performs competitively on geometric metrics and ranks among the best on physical ones. By unifying geometric and physical metrics under a polymorph-aware protocol, OPAL-Bench enables a more comprehensive assessment of generative quality in CSP.
